doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Jim and Andy's and the studio lifestyle
summary: Musicians hung out at Jim and Andy's below A&R Studios, and drinking could end careers in a surplus business.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Was there a certain place that you guys would hang in between?

Well Jim and Andy’s, and Charlie’s. Two spots. Then it evolved to Jim and Andy’s. It was on the first floor of the same building that A&R Records was, A&R Studios. So they were forever calling down “we need a trumpet player — we need a drummer” you know. There was always somebody down there. They’d run upstairs and do a record date.
I guess that’s a good reason for not like drinking too much while you’re there.
Wow. What was the lifestyle like? Were guys able to — I’m not sure how to put this — remain healthy?

Oh, well a lot of the guys were married and they lived on Long Island. There were very few single guys. So in order for them to make a living, I know the big thing was drinking in those days, more than anything else. And if they didn’t straighten out it caught up with them too soon and they were out of the business. Because once you screw up, being late or — they didn’t use you anymore. Because there were too many guys around. There were a lot of guys to pick from. It was really — we used to call it a surplus business. If
they couldn’t get you they got somebody else who played half as well as you did. They did the same job.
